{"questions": [
{
"id": "p1",
"topic": "combinatorics: subsets (arithmetic progressions)",
"error_type": "omitted_case",
"question": "How many 3-element subsets of {1, 2, …, 30} have the property that their elements form an arithmetic progression whose common difference is a prime number?",
"answer": 98,
"target_wrong": 94,
"error_description": "The case d = 13 is omitted: the progressions {1,14,27}, {2,15,28}, {3,16,29}, {4,17,30} (4 subsets) are missed because 2·13 = 26 barely fits inside 30.",
"cases": ["d=2: 26 subsets", "d=3: 24 subsets", "d=5: 20 subsets", "d=7: 16 subsets", "d=11: 8 subsets", "d=13: 4 subsets"],
"solution": "A 3-element arithmetic progression is {a, a+d, a+2d} with a ≥ 1 and a+2d ≤ 30, so for a fixed difference d there are 30 − 2d choices of a. We need d prime with 2d ≤ 29, i.e., d ∈ {2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13} (d = 17 gives 2d = 34 > 29). The counts are 30−4 = 26, 30−6 = 24, 30−10 = 20, 30−14 = 16, 30−22 = 8, 30−26 = 4. Summing: 26 + 24 + 20 + 16 + 8 + 4 = 98.",
"check_code": "from itertools import combinations\ndef is_prime(k):\n    return k > 1 and all(k % p for p in range(2, int(k**0.5) + 1))\ncnt = 0\nfor a, b, c in combinations(range(1, 31), 3):\n    if b - a == c - b and is_prime(b - a):\n        cnt += 1\nprint(cnt)"
},
{
"id": "p2",
"topic": "combinatorics: set partitions",
"error_type": "omitted_case",
"question": "In how many ways can the set {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8} be partitioned into blocks so that every block contains at least two elements? (The blocks are unordered.)",
"answer": 715,
"target_wrong": 680,
"error_description": "The block-size pattern 4+4 is omitted from the list of partitions of 8 into parts of size at least 2; it contributes C(8,4)/2 = 35 set partitions.",
"cases": ["8: 1", "6+2: C(8,2)=28", "5+3: C(8,3)=56", "4+4: C(8,4)/2=35", "4+2+2: C(8,4)·C(4,2)/2=210", "3+3+2: C(8,2)·C(6,3)/2=280", "2+2+2+2: 8!/(2^4·4!)=105"],
"solution": "List the partitions of the integer 8 into parts of size at least 2 and count set partitions of each shape. 8: 1 way. 6+2: C(8,2) = 28. 5+3: C(8,3) = 56. 4+4: C(8,4)/2 = 35 (the two blocks of equal size are interchangeable). 4+2+2: C(8,4)·C(4,2)/2 = 70·6/2 = 210. 3+3+2: C(8,2)·C(6,3)/2 = 28·20/2 = 280. 2+2+2+2: 8!/(2^4·4!) = 105. Total: 1 + 28 + 56 + 35 + 210 + 280 + 105 = 715.",
"check_code": "def partitions(s):\n    if not s:\n        yield []\n        return\n    first, rest = s[0], s[1:]\n    for p in partitions(rest):\n        for i in range(len(p)):\n            yield p[:i] + [[first] + p[i]] + p[i+1:]\n        yield [[first]] + p\ncnt = sum(1 for p in partitions(list(range(8))) if all(len(b) >= 2 for b in p))\nprint(cnt)"
},
{
"id": "p3",
"topic": "combinatorics: 2-element subsets and divisors",
"error_type": "omitted_case",
"question": "Find the sum of the positive integers n for which the number of 2-element subsets of {1, 2, …, n} is a positive divisor of 420.",
"answer": 71,
"target_wrong": 56,
"error_description": "The case n = 15 is omitted: C(15,2) = 105 divides 420 (420 = 4·105), but 105 is easily missed when scanning the divisors of 420 for triangular numbers.",
"cases": ["n=2: C=1", "n=3: C=3", "n=4: C=6", "n=5: C=10", "n=6: C=15", "n=7: C=21", "n=8: C=28", "n=15: C=105", "n=21: C=210"],
"solution": "We need C(n,2) = n(n−1)/2 to be a positive divisor of 420 = 2^2·3·5·7. The divisors of 420 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 10, 12, 14, 15, 20, 21, 28, 30, 35, 42, 60, 70, 84, 105, 140, 210, 420. The triangular numbers among them are 1 (n=2), 3 (n=3), 6 (n=4), 10 (n=5), 15 (n=6), 21 (n=7), 28 (n=8), 105 (n=15, since 15·14/2 = 105) and 210 (n=21, since 21·20/2 = 210). One checks 36, 45, 55, 66, 78, 91, 120, 136, 153, 171, 190, 231, …, 406 are not divisors, and 420 itself is not triangular (29·28 = 812, 30·29 = 870 ≠ 840). Sum: 2+3+4+5+6+7+8+15+21 = 71.",
"check_code": "from math import comb\nprint(sum(n for n in range(1, 200) if comb(n, 2) > 0 and 420 % comb(n, 2) == 0))"
},
{
"id": "p4",
"topic": "combinatorics: subsets with sum condition (residue classes)",
"error_type": "omitted_case",
"question": "How many 3-element subsets of {1, 2, …, 16} have the property that the sum of their elements is divisible by 5?",
"answer": 112,
"target_wrong": 103,
"error_description": "The residue pattern {3,3,4} (two elements ≡ 3 and one ≡ 4 mod 5, sum ≡ 10) is omitted; it contributes C(3,2)·3 = 9 subsets.",
"cases": ["{0,0,0}: C(3,3)=1", "{0,1,4}: 3·4·3=36", "{0,2,3}: 3·3·3=27", "{1,1,3}: C(4,2)·3=18", "{2,2,1}: C(3,2)·4=12", "{3,3,4}: C(3,2)·3=9", "{4,4,2}: C(3,2)·3=9"],
"solution": "Residues mod 5 in {1,…,16}: class 0 = {5,10,15} (3 numbers), class 1 = {1,6,11,16} (4), class 2 = {2,7,12} (3), class 3 = {3,8,13} (3), class 4 = {4,9,14} (3). A multiset of three residues sums to 0 mod 5 exactly in these cases: {0,0,0}: C(3,3) = 1; {0,1,4}: 3·4·3 = 36; {0,2,3}: 3·3·3 = 27; {1,1,3}: C(4,2)·3 = 18; {1,2,2}: 4·C(3,2) = 12; {3,3,4}: C(3,2)·3 = 9; {2,4,4}: 3·C(3,2) = 9. (The triples {1,1,1}, {2,2,2}, {3,3,3}, {4,4,4} have sums 3, 6, 9, 12, none ≡ 0.) Total: 1 + 36 + 27 + 18 + 12 + 9 + 9 = 112.",
"check_code": "from itertools import combinations\nprint(sum(1 for s in combinations(range(1, 17), 3) if sum(s) % 5 == 0))"
},
{
"id": "p5",
"topic": "combinatorics: selections of lattice points",
"error_type": "omitted_case",
"question": "The 25 points (x, y) with x, y ∈ {0, 1, 2, 3, 4} form a square array. How many ways are there to choose 4 of these points so that they are the vertices of a square?",
"answer": 50,
"target_wrong": 48,
"error_description": "The tilted squares with side vector (1,3) or (3,1) are omitted; each has a 4×4 bounding box and fits in exactly one position, contributing 2 squares.",
"cases": ["axis-aligned side 1: 16", "axis-aligned side 2: 9", "axis-aligned side 3: 4", "axis-aligned side 4: 1", "tilted side vector (1,1): 9", "tilted side vectors (1,2) and (2,1): 4+4=8", "tilted side vectors (1,3) and (3,1): 1+1=2", "tilted side vector (2,2): 1"],
"solution": "A square with one side given by the vector (a,b), a ≥ 1, b ≥ 0, has an axis-aligned bounding box of side a+b, so it can be placed in (5 − (a+b))^2 positions provided a+b ≤ 4. Axis-aligned squares (b = 0): a = 1,2,3,4 give 16, 9, 4, 1 → 30. Tilted squares (a,b ≥ 1): (1,1): bounding box 2, 3^2 = 9 positions; (1,2) and (2,1): bounding box 3, 2^2 = 4 each → 8; (1,3) and (3,1): bounding box 4, 1 each → 2; (2,2): bounding box 4, 1 position. Tilted total 9 + 8 + 2 + 1 = 20. Altogether 30 + 20 = 50.",
"check_code": "from itertools import combinations\npts = [(x, y) for x in range(5) for y in range(5)]\ndef is_square(q):\n    d = sorted((p[0]-r[0])**2 + (p[1]-r[1])**2 for p, r in combinations(q, 2))\n    return d[0] > 0 and d[0] == d[1] == d[2] == d[3] and d[4] == d[5] == 2 * d[0]\nprint(sum(1 for q in combinations(pts, 4) if is_square(q)))"
},
{
"id": "p6",
"topic": "combinatorics: subsets (size equals minimum)",
"error_type": "omitted_case",
"question": "How many nonempty subsets S of {1, 2, …, 12} have the property that the number of elements of S is equal to the smallest element of S?",
"answer": 144,
"target_wrong": 138,
"error_description": "The case min(S) = 6 is omitted: S must have 6 elements with smallest element 6, so the other 5 are chosen from {7,…,12}, giving C(6,5) = 6 subsets.",
"cases": ["min=1: C(11,0)=1", "min=2: C(10,1)=10", "min=3: C(9,2)=36", "min=4: C(8,3)=56", "min=5: C(7,4)=35", "min=6: C(6,5)=6"],
"solution": "Let m = min(S) = |S|. Then S contains m and m−1 further elements chosen from {m+1, …, 12}, a set of 12 − m elements, so there are C(12−m, m−1) such subsets. This is nonzero only when m−1 ≤ 12−m, i.e., m ≤ 6. m=1: C(11,0) = 1; m=2: C(10,1) = 10; m=3: C(9,2) = 36; m=4: C(8,3) = 56; m=5: C(7,4) = 35; m=6: C(6,5) = 6. Total: 1 + 10 + 36 + 56 + 35 + 6 = 144.",
"check_code": "cnt = 0\nfor mask in range(1, 1 << 12):\n    s = [i + 1 for i in range(12) if mask >> i & 1]\n    if len(s) == min(s):\n        cnt += 1\nprint(cnt)"
},
{
"id": "p7",
"topic": "combinatorics: counting subsets of a set of unknown size",
"error_type": "algebra_slip",
"question": "The number of 3-element subsets of a finite set S is exactly 57 times the number of elements of S. How many 2-element subsets does S have?",
"answer": 190,
"target_wrong": 136,
"error_description": "After reducing to (n−1)(n−2) = 342, the expansion is written as n² + 3n + 2 = 342 (sign slip on the linear term), giving n² + 3n − 340 = (n+20)(n−17) = 0, so n = 17 and C(17,2) = 136 instead of n = 20 and C(20,2) = 190.",
"cases": [],
"solution": "Let |S| = n. Then C(n,3) = 57n gives n(n−1)(n−2)/6 = 57n, so (n−1)(n−2) = 342. Expanding, n² − 3n + 2 = 342, i.e., n² − 3n − 340 = 0, which factors as (n − 20)(n + 17) = 0. Hence n = 20 (check: C(20,3) = 1140 = 57·20). The number of 2-element subsets is C(20,2) = 190.",
"check_code": "from math import comb\nfor n in range(3, 1000):\n    if comb(n, 3) == 57 * n:\n        print(comb(n, 2))\n        break"
},
{
"id": "p8",
"topic": "combinatorics: subsets with a selection constraint",
"error_type": "misread_condition",
"question": "How many 4-element subsets of {1, 2, …, 12} contain at least two multiples of 3?",
"answer": 201,
"target_wrong": 168,
"error_description": "The condition 'at least two multiples of 3' is read as 'exactly two multiples of 3', giving only C(4,2)·C(8,2) = 168 and dropping the subsets with three or four multiples of 3.",
"cases": [],
"solution": "The multiples of 3 in {1,…,12} are 3, 6, 9, 12 (4 numbers); the other 8 numbers are not multiples of 3. A 4-element subset with exactly k multiples of 3 can be chosen in C(4,k)·C(8,4−k) ways. We need k ≥ 2: k=2: C(4,2)·C(8,2) = 6·28 = 168; k=3: C(4,3)·C(8,1) = 4·8 = 32; k=4: C(4,4)·C(8,0) = 1. Total 168 + 32 + 1 = 201.",
"check_code": "from itertools import combinations\nprint(sum(1 for s in combinations(range(1, 13), 4) if sum(1 for x in s if x % 3 == 0) >= 2))"
},
{
"id": "p9",
"topic": "combinatorics: subsets (inclusion–exclusion)",
"error_type": "double_counting",
"question": "How many subsets of {1, 2, …, 10} contain at least one even number and at least one multiple of 3?",
"answer": 872,
"target_wrong": 864,
"error_description": "In the inclusion–exclusion count 2^10 − 2^5 − 2^7 + 2^3, the subsets with no even number and no multiple of 3 (the 8 subsets of {1,5,7}) are subtracted twice but never added back, giving 1024 − 32 − 128 = 864.",
"cases": [],
"solution": "There are 2^10 = 1024 subsets in total. Let A be the set of subsets with no even number: these are subsets of the 5 odd numbers, 2^5 = 32 of them. Let B be the set of subsets with no multiple of 3: subsets of {1,2,4,5,7,8,10}, 2^7 = 128 of them. Subsets in both A and B are subsets of the numbers that are odd and not multiples of 3, namely {1, 5, 7}: 2^3 = 8. By inclusion–exclusion the number of subsets lacking an even number or lacking a multiple of 3 is 32 + 128 − 8 = 152, so the answer is 1024 − 152 = 872.",
"check_code": "cnt = 0\nfor mask in range(1 << 10):\n    s = [i + 1 for i in range(10) if mask >> i & 1]\n    if any(x % 2 == 0 for x in s) and any(x % 3 == 0 for x in s):\n        cnt += 1\nprint(cnt)"
},
{
"id": "p10",
"topic": "combinatorics: subsets with bounded spread",
"error_type": "off_by_one",
"question": "How many nonempty subsets of {1, 2, …, 15} have the property that the largest element minus the smallest element is at most 6?",
"answer": 639,
"target_wrong": 624,
"error_description": "The one-element subsets, for which largest minus smallest equals 0, are left out: the count starts the difference d at 1 instead of 0, missing the 15 singletons.",
"cases": [],
"solution": "Classify a nonempty subset by its minimum a and maximum b, and let d = b − a. If d = 0 the subset is a singleton: 15 subsets. If d ≥ 1, the pair (a, b) can be chosen in 15 − d ways, and the d − 1 integers strictly between a and b may each be included or not, giving 2^(d−1) subsets per pair. For d = 1,…,6 this gives 14·1 + 13·2 + 12·4 + 11·8 + 10·16 + 9·32 = 14 + 26 + 48 + 88 + 160 + 288 = 624. Adding the 15 singletons gives 624 + 15 = 639.",
"check_code": "cnt = 0\nfor mask in range(1, 1 << 15):\n    s = [i + 1 for i in range(15) if mask >> i & 1]\n    if max(s) - min(s) <= 6:\n        cnt += 1\nprint(cnt)"
}
]}
